ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: All kinds of rock (soil) whose temperature is at 0°C or below 0°C and that contain ice are called frozen soil. Read the following figure, "Profile of Permafrost Distribution in the Northern Hemisphere," and answer the following questions. <image1> The figure shows that, in the middle latitudes, what characteristic does the thickness of permafrost have as latitude changes?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: First describe the image: The figure is a profile of permafrost distribution in the Northern Hemisphere. Horizontally it marks latitudes such as 80°, 70°, 60°, 50°, and 40°. The left side is higher latitude and the right side is lower latitude; the shaded part represents permafrost. In the figure, the permafrost layer is thicker on the high-latitude side and gradually becomes thinner toward the middle- and low-latitude direction. Near 50°–40°, the permafrost is very thin or becomes sporadic or seasonal frozen soil. Then reason: Within the middle-latitude range, when moving from lower latitude to higher latitude, the thickness of the permafrost shaded layer shown in the figure gradually increases; therefore the thickness of middle-latitude permafrost thickens as latitude increases.

method.method_draft: 先描述图像：图示为北半球多年冻土分布剖面，横向标有40°—80°纬度，右低左高，阴影表示多年冻土。再聚焦中纬度范围，从较低纬度的40°—50°附近看多年冻土很薄或呈季节冻土、零散冻土；向60°、70°方向移动时，标注“多年冻土”的阴影层明显加厚。由此概括：中纬度多年冻土厚度随纬度增高而增厚。
